contentBlocks.text: A 4-year-old girl with a known chronic haemolytic anaemia is brought to the emergency department with fatigue and loss of appetite. Her parents first noticed her fatigue 3 days ago when she asked to go to sleep earlier than her bedtime. Over the past 2 days the patient has been drinking well but eating much less than normal. Her father states, "She's been so tired that she wouldn't even get out of bed this morning." She had an episode of acute chest syndrome 2 years prior that required an exchange transfusion. The patient takes folic acid and penicillin. Immunizations are up to date, including the annual influenza vaccine. Temperature is 36.7 C (98 F), blood pressure is 110/65 mm Hg, pulse is 120/min, and respirations are 25/min. Oxygen saturation is 95% on room air. Physical examination shows a pale and tired-appearing girl. Conjunctival pallor is present. Respiratory, abdominal, and neurologic examinations are within normal limits. Laboratory results are as follows:
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis of this patient?

questions.explanation: FIXTURE EXPLANATION. The distinguishing feature in this vignette is the reticulocyte count of 0.1%: a marrow that has stopped producing red cells despite profound anaemia. Haemolytic and sequestration processes would be expected to drive the reticulocyte count up rather than down.
questions.educationalObjective: FIXTURE OBJECTIVE. Use the reticulocyte response to separate production failure from increased destruction or pooling.

questions.stem:
A 62-year-old man is evaluated for a 6-month history of progressive exertional dyspnoea. Examination reveals a mid-systolic murmur at the right upper sternal border radiating to the carotids, with a delayed and diminished carotid upstroke.

Which of the following findings would be most consistent with the suspected diagnosis?

options.label: B
options.text: Dilated left atrium with normal ventricular wall thickness

Which of the following are appropriate components of the initial assessment? (Select three.)

questions.explanation: FIXTURE EXPLANATION. Multiple-select fixture with eight options. Grading requires the selected set to exactly equal {A, B, D}; a partial match is not credited.
questions.educationalObjective: FIXTURE OBJECTIVE. Demonstrates select-three grading across an A–H option list.

questions.stem:
A 54-year-old man with a 30-pack-year smoking history presents with 4 months of progressive dyspnoea on exertion and a chronic productive cough. He reports three exacerbations in the past year, each treated with oral corticosteroids. He has no orthopnoea and no lower-limb oedema. Temperature is 36.9 C (98.4 F), blood pressure is 128/78 mm Hg, pulse is 88/min, and respirations are 20/min. Oxygen saturation is 93% on room air. Examination shows a barrel-shaped chest, diminished breath sounds bilaterally, and a prolonged expiratory phase. Spirometry after bronchodilator shows an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.58 with an FEV1 of 55% predicted.

Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in long-term management?

suggestedHighlights.note: Principal risk factor stated in the stem.

suggestedHighlights.text: three exacerbations in the past year

questions.explanation: FIXTURE EXPLANATION. Long-stem fixture that also carries suggestedHighlights supplied by the upstream pipeline.
